mission.display_title: Place continuous families beside discrete ones
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to extend yesterday's discrete recognition into continuous univariate families. So you can characterise Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, and continuous uniform by support and typical use, without pretending probability evaluation is finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to discriminate continuous families by support and modelling role, and to refuse treating 'everything is Normal' as a default without warrant. So continuous entry matches the same Sensei standard as discrete entry.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'continuous = Normal only' to 'I can place the syllabus continuous families by support and typical actuarial/statistical role, with one honest non-default.'
mission.learning_objective: Describe the characteristics of Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, and uniform continuous distributions on an interval, and match key members to recognisable modelling situations.
mission.concept_focus: Support / shape story → continuous family → refuse Normal-by-default theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you matched discrete counting situations to 2.1.1 families. Today the same 2.1 topic continues at 2.1.2: continuous univariate characteristics sit beside the discrete map. Not a new chapter leap.
mission.why_now: You've placed discrete families; today place continuous ones beside them so you don't default every continuous problem to Normal.
mission.expected_benefit: A continuous-family placement map with one refused Normal default. Study Progress for today's Session, not Topic Complete for 2.1.3–2.1.6.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Beta Day 3 because contiguous 2.1.1→2.1.2 completes lawful distributional entry without swallowing probability evaluation and generation LOs.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: continuous family roster
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names the Syllabus 2.1.2 continuous families and gives support or role cues for Normal, lognormal, exponential, and gamma?
knowledge_checks.body: Select roster plus core placement cues.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Continuous entry requires roster and core placement cues before calculation days.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Name the continuous families; cue Normal, lognormal, exponential, and gamma by support or modelling role.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Naming only Normal, or dumping formulae without placement cues.

choices.label: Families include Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, and continuous uniform. Cues: Normal for symmetric continuous approximation; lognormal for positive skewed magnitudes; exponential for waiting or memoryless times; gamma for flexible positive continuous shapes.
Only Normal is needed in 2.1.2; other continuous families are optional names without placement cues.
Normal has strictly positive support, lognormal is symmetric on all reals, exponential is for without-replacement counts, and gamma is only for probabilities on (0,1).
The continuous roster is geometric, binomial, negative binomial, hypergeometric, Poisson, and discrete uniform.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: place and refuse Normal default
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Individual claim sizes are strictly positive and right-skewed. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Prefer a positive skewed family; refuse Normal-by-default.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Continuous judgement refuses Normal theatre for positive skewed claim sizes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prefer lognormal or gamma; refuse Normal on support and skew grounds for individual claim sizes.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Default Normal because of the CLT without addressing support and skew of the individual size.

choices.label: Start with lognormal or gamma because claim sizes are strictly positive and right-skewed. Refuse Normal-by-default because a symmetric all-real support model mismatches the support and skew of the quantity.
Use Normal by default because the central limit theorem always makes individual claim sizes Normal.
Use continuous uniform on all reals because positive skew is irrelevant once a continuous family is chosen.
Refuse lognormal and gamma for positive skewed sizes, and prefer Normal specifically because it cannot produce negative draws in practice.

worked_example.title: Select Lognormal for positive right-skewed severities
worked_example.problem_statement: Individual claim severities are strictly positive and strongly right-skewed on the raw scale, with a roughly symmetric shape after taking logs. Choose the matching continuous family. As a light numeric check, if ln(X) ~ Normal(μ = 6, σ = 1), compute the median of X.

given.value: strictly positive, right-skewed severities; approximately Normal on the log scale

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Match support and log-scale shape to a named continuous family before evaluating the median.

steps.label: Match story to family
steps.attempt_cue: Name the continuous family for positive right-skewed sizes that are Normal on the log scale.
steps.explanation: Lognormal models strictly positive variables that are approximately Normal after a log transform and typically right-skewed on the raw scale. Normal on the raw scale allows negatives and is a poor default for severities.
steps.calculation: Story → Lognormal (refuse Normal-by-default on raw severity)

steps.label: Light numeric illustration of the median
steps.explanation: If ln(X) is Normal(μ, σ), the median of X is e^μ because the Normal median equals μ. The numeric check illustrates the chosen family; family selection remains the LO hinge.

steps.label: Refuse Normal-by-default
steps.attempt_cue: State the support mismatch for a raw-scale Normal severity model.
steps.explanation: A Normal model on the raw scale allows negative severities and does not encode the stated log-scale symmetry. That mismatches the positive right-skewed severity story.
steps.calculation: Normal raw support includes negatives → refuse as first match

worked_example.final_answer: Choose Lognormal for positive right-skewed severities that are Normal on the log scale; with ln(X) ~ Normal(6, 1), median(X) = e^6 ≈ 403.43. Refuse Normal-by-default on the raw severity scale.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Defaulting to a Normal severity model because it is familiar, ignoring that claim sizes are strictly positive and right-skewed on the raw scale.
